summary: Boundary County lookout: log cabin 1930, pole tower 1936, abandoned 1958 per Idaho sources; footings and a cabin reported on the peak; a Forest Service trail leads there.

facts.design: Log cabin (1930), then a pole tower (1936)
facts.status_note: Tower gone; footings and a decaying cabin reported on the summit in an undated hiking write-up

access.note: Forest Service lists Trail #236 to the peak as a recreation trail; no closure reported in these sources

visit.trail_note: About one mile of single-track from the official trailhead of Trail #236 to the summit, per a hiking write-up

events.note: Dan Kimball, first staff member named in the sources
Idaho Fire Lookouts and Idaho Magazine give 1958; firelookout.com lists staff for 1960-1961
Durward Stolp listed for 1960-1961 on firelookout.com; conflicts with the 1958 abandonment year
firelookout.com says gone by 1964; no removal date given

evidence.supports: log cabin 1930 with ruins, pole tower 1936, gone by 1964
evidence.quote: 1930: log cabin (ruins still there). 1936: pole tower. Gone by 1964.

evidence.supports: location nine miles west of Bonners Ferry, Boundary County

evidence.quote: Known lookout personnel: 1932: Dan Kimball; 1933-1935: Evan Watson; 1936: Robert Saarf; 1956: Paul Weber; 1958: Bruce Baker; 1959: Tim Jones; 1960-1961: Durward Stolp.
In 1936 a pole tower was constructed and remained in use until the lookout was abandoned in 1958.

evidence.supports: initially a log cabin built in 1930
evidence.quote: The fire lookout on Cooks Peak was initially a log cabin that was built in 1930.

evidence.supports: Forest Service trail to the peak; site of old lookout and cabin at the summit
evidence.quote: At the peak you will find the site of the old fire lookout and cabin.

evidence.supports: footings of the tower intact and a decaying cabin (undated write-up)
evidence.quote: It is a former fire lookout, with the footings of the tower still intact and a decaying cabin rapidly disappearing.

evidence.supports: about one mile of single-track from official trailhead to the peak
evidence.quote: From this point it is one mile to the peak on a single-track

evidence.supports: Walter Peel manned the lookout (Bonners Ferry Herald, 2024 column)
the column recalls the early 1930s, when lookouts in Boundary County were manned
evidence.quote: In the early 1930s, many lookouts were being constructed and manned by Civilian Conservation Corps men in Boundary County.

evidence.supports: trail about one mile long (Forest Service)
evidence.quote: The Cooks Peak Trail #236 is approximately 1 mile long.
Shortly after you’ll end up at the official trailhead for trail #236.

sources.title: Cooks Peak Trail #236
sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service, Idaho Panhandle National Forests

corrections.why: The tower is gone, but NaughtyHiker reports its footings still intact and the cabin decaying, and the Forest Service page describes the summit as the site of the old lookout and cabin. The vocabulary's 'ruins' means footings or remains only. The NaughtyHiker write-up is undated, so the editor should confirm the footings are still there.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts and Idaho Magazine give 1958; firelookout.com lists staff in 1960 and 1961 and says the tower was gone by 1964. The record and story use 1958 as the abandonment year, cite both, and flag the later staff entries rather than choosing between them.

notes_for_editor: Location conflict not resolved here: FFLA gives 48.70696, -116.5349 and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 48.70854, -116.55715 (about 1.6 km apart). The record keeps the FFLA point. The NaughtyHiker write-up is undated on the page and its comments run to August 2017, so the footings claim may be out of date. Staffing as_of 1961 is the last named staff member, not an abandonment date. No new photos found.
